workstream.name: ecl v1 — the real interpreter (design/workstream-v1.md)
workstream.unlocks: M9 can run blocking http work without changing the task/outcome interface, and M10 can treat scheduler determinism, cancellation, structured teardown, and worker-safe snapshot reclamation as settled acceptance infrastructure.

problemStatement: M6 leaves ecl with an explicitly framed evaluator and poll-bounded traversals, but every Unit still runs synchronously on its caller, task is absent from the Value/HeapKind surface, cancellation is one Session-wide boolean reported as a user error, and output writers and mutable runtime services are not safe for concurrent units. Environment shapes and registry directories also retain every superseded snapshot until teardown, so enabling long-lived parallel sessions without M7 would add data races, finite-pool deadlocks, unbounded metadata growth, and orphaned work.
solutionSummary: First make the existing shared publication paths worker-safe: use blocking host mutexes where spinning would burn workers, add reader leases and reclamation for environment/registry snapshots, and synchronize provenance publication without relocating accumulated state. Then make Unit heap-stable and resumable, add identity task values, and build one lazily started fixed worker pool with an intrusive typed work queue, write-once task cells, per-park wait sets, single-winner wake-policy transitions, and a session-root structured task tree. Expose spawn/await/cancel/tasks, then await-any and await-for through defunctionalized machine continuations so a waiting unit parks instead of blocking a worker; one lazy timer thread owns a non-relocating binary heap. Finally source-define par-each, serialize each complete console write, and run behavioral/OOM/TSan/release acceptance at one and many workers while preserving a zero-worker cold start.

mergabilityStrategy.featureFlagStrategy: Ship ungated. Concurrency is a missing v1 language surface with no persisted state or deployed compatibility population. ECL_WORKERS is ordinary scheduler configuration, not a rollout flag: every supported positive value has the same language semantics, and the test matrix must prove that rather than maintaining two modes.
mergabilityStrategy.patchOrderingStrategy: Patch 1 is a non-functional shared-state hardening patch and introduces all pending behavioral proof names. Patch 2 adds the task/value and resumable-Unit representation without installing task words. Patch 3 adds the lazy pool, structured control blocks, wait sets, and locked console behind that unreachable seam. Patch 4 is the first public behavior patch and installs spawn/await/cancel/tasks. Patch 5 adds the racing and deadline operations on the same wait-set protocol. Patch 6 adds source par-each, CLI worker configuration, the complete worker-count/acceptance matrix, documentation, and final source-budget enforcement. The dependency chain is deliberately linear across scheduler.zig and the shared test file so no two branches invent incompatible state machines in parallel.

currentStateAnalysis: Grounded on clean master at 86d7cfe, synchronized with origin/master; M6 is committed at 214078d and its completed gameplan has been removed. Session.executeParsed creates a stack-local machine.Unit, calls machine.run to exhaustion, then moves the stack back; Machine.loop owns current evaluator state on the host stack and its fuel/kernel polls only inspect one Session.cancelled flag. Value.Tag has int/float/char/symbol/word/list/dict, HeapKind has nine non-task members, heap release switches know only list/dict children, type omits task, and equal/print/hash have no identity-object case. Scope has a mutable tagged storage union and raw parent pointer, so a transient isolated scope cannot safely outlive its frame or publish its lazy Environment pointer to a child worker. Session owns unsynchronized writer pointers and a shared SpanArchive; pp/prin, which/see, shadow diagnostics, and main's prompt/stack output write through separate paths. Environment Shape and Registry Directory form previous chains destroyed only at teardown, while BindingCell generations already demonstrate a reader-counted retirement pattern. Registry and Environment writers plus the process intern table use std.atomic.Mutex tryLock spin loops; M7 specifically requires the intern writer to become blocking before parallel parse. The build is pinned to Zig 0.16.0, whose available blocking primitive is std.Io.Mutex (with std.Io.Threaded mutex helpers or an Io value), and std.Thread supplies getCpuCount/spawn/join. Under the business-logic-only policy, the source audit baseline is 15,015/22,000 shipped Zig lines, excluding tests, fixtures, build/source-audit verification tooling, and every .ecl source; it has no scheduler component, leaving 6,985 total lines if scheduler/task/console receives one new <=3,500-line business-logic component and the overall 22,000 ceiling is not raised. Tests live under src/tests, real-binary tests under test/e2e.zig, the full initialized-Session OOM sweep under src/tests/oom_test.zig, and architecture constraints belong in uncapped src/tools/source_audit.zig rather than tests that read implementation source.

operationalConsiderations.externalSystemAccess: No network, database, queue, credential, or new filesystem authority is added. The new external resources are local OS worker threads, one local timer thread, the process monotonic clock, and the existing stdout/stderr handles. src/main.zig owns ECL_WORKERS parsing and passes a validated positive count into Session.Config; Session/Scheduler owns thread creation and joins every created thread during deinit. Worker- or timer-thread creation and unavailable clock facilities become ordinary 'io language failures at the initiating word; there is no ambient fallback pool and no detached thread.
operationalConsiderations.crossRuntimeContracts: The only new process-boundary input is ECL_WORKERS, parsed as a base-10 positive usize with invalid/zero/overflow values rejected before Session construction. Both str and pp render a task as the verbatim opaque marker <task:N>, where N is a monotone per-Session display ID that remains stable and is not reused during that Session. The reader rejects that runtime-only marker wherever it occurs, so a task or any rendered structure containing one is intentionally unparseable; there is no escaping, surrogate serialization, or session-local lookup. DESIGN d.16's canonical reader round-trip is narrowed to values that contain no session-linked runtime objects. The frozen Rust oracle has no concurrency and remains untouched; M7 behavior is proved natively through the Zig library and release binary. stdout retains UTF-8 bytes and existing canonical value rendering, but each prin/pp/which/see/main write becomes indivisible with respect to other units.
operationalConsiderations.failureBehavior: spawn prevalidates a quotation and completes all allocations, parent registration, and kill-on-arrival checks before exposing a handle; allocation failure remains host OutOfMemory and OS thread startup failure is 'io. A child language failure is cached as the same {'err error-dict} shape as attempt; child OutOfMemory is a distinct terminal cell state and propagates OutOfMemory through await rather than fabricating a language error. exit is process control owned by the root Unit outside attempt: a spawned Unit or any invocation inside attempt receives an ordinary catchable 'domain failure instead of setting Session.requested_exit, while an allowed root exit first closes, cancels, and quiesces the root task scope before the Session returns its status to the CLI. cancel is allocation-free after registration, recursively flags descendants, wins or loses the current park token exactly once, removes waiter/timer registrations, and is a no-op for an already terminal task. await-for requires a non-negative integer duration; an already terminal task wins before a zero deadline, otherwise timeout returns {'err {'kind 'timeout ...}} without cancelling the task. await-any prevalidates a nonempty list and every task before registration; already-complete ties choose the lowest list index, while genuinely concurrent completion is the specified nondeterministic case. Session and task-scope close cancel outstanding descendants and wait for quiescence even after language failure, cancellation, exit, or OOM. No cleanup or wake path allocates.
operationalConsiderations.concurrencyAndIdempotency: Scheduler ownership is per Session. A single mutex/condition protects an intrusive FIFO of typed task, wait-cleanup, and value-release jobs; the scheduler core makes every ready/running/parked/closing/done transition and prevents duplicate execution. Every user-sized traversal has one cursor implementation and a scheduler-attached cursor preserves its exact position and partial result before yielding within the accounted-work quantum. There is no cancellation-only or unlimited legacy traversal mode. Each task cell has a small blocking mutex, one terminal state, ordered child links, and waiter links; task completion publishes the immutable outcome with Release/Acquire visibility and detaches waiters in bounded slices. Each await operation allocates one exact-size, non-relocating registration array plus an exact non-rehashing duplicate directory. Completion, timeout, and cancellation race through one wait policy; the winner schedules resumable loser unlinking and task-handle retirement before enqueueing the owner. Parent child lists are mutexed, spawn registers then rechecks parent cancellation (kill-on-arrival), and child completion unlinks before notifying quiescence. Environment/registry snapshot leases prevent reclamation while a reader traverses, writers retire under their existing publication locks, and final reader release or a later writer advances bounded reclamation. Output locks cover one logical call, not each chunk. Await is read-only/idempotent after completion; cancel and repeated completion attempts are no-ops/asserted impossible; timeout does not mutate the task.
operationalConsiderations.rollbackStrategy: No persistent schema, external data, or irreversible operator action exists. Each patch leaves Session teardown able to stop/join only the resources introduced so far. Revert in reverse order: remove par-each/matrix/docs, timer/race words, basic task words, scheduler/console, task/resumable representation, then snapshot/locking hardening. Task IDs, pending cells, timer entries, and worker queues are process memory only and are destroyed at Session teardown; a binary downgrade sees no migrated artifact.

functionalChanges.description: spawn consumes one quotation, returns a first-class identity task handle, and runs the quotation on an empty isolated stack/scope on a lazily started fixed worker pool; type reports 'task, match/dict-key hashing use handle identity, str and pp render stable per-Session <task:N> markers, and parse rejects those markers rather than reconstructing live state.

await parks the current green Unit without occupying a worker and later returns the cached attempt-shaped outcome; any number of duplicated handles/waiters may await the same cell and repeated await is idempotent.

cancel is a no-op for terminal tasks and otherwise recursively cancels the target and descendants, wakes a parked target at most once, removes its waiter registrations, and ultimately caches a standard 'cancelled error outcome with target trace information when available.

tasks returns a deterministic spawn-order snapshot of pending descendants in the current task scope; the REPL Session is the persistent root scope, while a spawned task cannot publish its own outcome until every unawaited descendant is cancelled and quiescent.

await-any prevalidates a nonempty list of tasks, returns the winning zero-based index plus cached outcome, chooses the lowest index among tasks already complete at registration time, and permits scheduler timing to choose only among later concurrent completions.

await-for accepts a task and nonnegative integer milliseconds, returns the task outcome if it is already/first complete, otherwise returns a standard 'timeout error outcome at the deadline without cancelling or completing the task; it uses one lazy timer thread for the Session.

Fuel exhaustion yields runnable Units back to the global queue and every user-sized traversal has one cursor implementation that can suspend at its exact bounded position; cancellation remains observable within 65,536 logical elements even inside flat kernels and one-worker execution cannot be monopolized indefinitely by a finite native traversal.

pp, prin, which, see, shadow diagnostics, stack display, and REPL/CLI prompts hold a shared Session console lock for one complete logical write, so different tasks may reorder whole calls but never interleave their bytes or race a buffered writer.

Source-defined par-each runs one isolated application per input, returns results in input order, enforces one result per element, and on failure rethrows the leftmost indexed error only after cancelling and quiescing every later sibling.

ECL_WORKERS selects any positive fixed worker count (including 1), invalid values fail before execution, no worker or timer thread is created before the first spawn/timed wait, and all deterministic corpus outcomes agree at one and eight workers.

exit may request process termination only from the root Unit outside attempt; a spawned Unit or attempt-contained call raises catchable 'domain, while an allowed root exit cancels and quiesces every outstanding descendant before returning its status to the CLI.

contextResources.why: The settled d.19/d.20/d.23 outcome, structured lifetime, publication, safe-point, determinism, timer, IO, task-cell, M7 DoD, and source-prelude tier contracts.

The real 16-byte value/header layout, resumable RC destruction, identity-free structural operations, explicit cursor states, Unit fields, frame ownership, cancellation budgets, isolated applications, primitive contracts, and slice-driven run loop that the scheduler extends rather than bypasses.

The fixed intern segments, Shape/Directory previous chains, BindingCell/ModuleSlot reader protocols, consumable module/loading capabilities, Scope lazy publication, SpanArchive ownership, and Session lifetime order that must become worker-safe before public spawn.

The mandatory behavior-only test rule, test/source layout, single full-Session OOM topology, real-binary harness, named TSan step, current CI gates, parsed source-audit authority, and 22,000-line business-logic accounting that excludes tests, fixtures, verification tooling, and ECL source.

The grounded BEAM-reduction, parked-continuation, multi-waiter IVar, Trio/JEP structured lifetime, atomic RC, timer, finite-pool deadlock, double-wake, kill-on-arrival, and par-each grain analysis behind the workstream's corrected protocol.
Trio nursery lifetime grounds parent ownership, cancellation propagation, and wait-for-quiescence: a scope cannot report completion while descendant work is still live.

The repository pins Zig 0.16.0; scheduler code must use the inspected std.Io.Mutex, std.Io.Condition/futex, std.Thread.getCpuCount/spawn/join, and clock shapes from that exact standard library rather than a remembered older Zig API.

acceptanceCriteria: With no spawn, a Session reports zero scheduler worker threads and zero timer threads; the release command `ecl '3 4 +'` prints `7`, exits 0, and does not initialize the pool.
`(1 2 +) spawn dup await pop await or-raise call` prints `3`; two different waiters and repeated awaits receive structurally identical cached outcomes without blocking the sole worker.

A task handle reports type 'task, matches only duplicate handles, works as a dict key under whole-value has?/at, remains inert inside lists, and both str and pp print its stable per-Session <task:N> marker without reading mutable task state; parse rejects that marker bare or inside any rendered enclosing structure, while the same bytes inside a string literal remain ordinary text.

`7 exit` and `(7 exit) call` in the root Unit exit with status 7 only after all root descendants are cancelled and quiescent; `(7 exit) attempt` and `(7 exit) spawn await` instead produce ordinary catchable 'domain outcomes and never set the Session process status.

A spawned quotation begins with an empty stack and a fresh disposable child scope whose parent bindings remain late-bound and readable; definitions in the child never leak into the parent, and values cross threads by existing atomic RC rather than copying.

Cancelling a CPU loop, a 70,000+-element native traversal, a unit parked in await, and a parent concurrently registering a child all terminate as `{'err {'kind 'cancelled ...}}`; every case wakes at most once, leaves no waiter/timer registration, and is quiescent before its owner scope closes.

tasks returns pending descendants in deterministic spawn preorder, excludes terminal tasks, persists root tasks across REPL runUnit calls, and a spawned task's terminal outcome is withheld until its own pending descendants have been cancelled and quiesced.

await-any rejects a non-list, empty list, or any non-task before registering anywhere; duplicate/already-done inputs choose the lowest zero-based index, while a controlled two-completer race returns exactly one index/outcome and enqueues its waiter exactly once.

await-for rejects non-integer/negative milliseconds, returns an already-done outcome even at 0ms, otherwise returns a standard timeout outcome at/after the monotonic deadline without cancelling the task; a later await can still receive that task's eventual outcome.

Only the first operation requiring it creates the timer thread; deadline insertion/removal uses a non-relocating chunked binary heap, earlier inserted deadlines wake the timer, cancelled/completed waits are removed, and Session deinit joins the timer without waiting for a far-future deadline.

Concurrent pp/prin/which/see/shadow/main output calls may appear in either call order but each call's exact bytes are contiguous; cancellation or IO failure releases the console lock and no buffered writer data race is reported by TSan.

`[1 2 3] (dup *) par-each` returns `[1 4 9]`; zero/multiple child results produce an indexed contract error; multiple failures rethrow the lowest input index after later siblings are cancelled/quiesced; outputs and errors are identical with ECL_WORKERS=1 and 8.
ECL_WORKERS accepts positive base-10 values including 1 and 8 and rejects missing digits, zero, signs, overflow, and trailing bytes with a stable CLI diagnostic before source execution.

A one-worker fairness probe with two long finite native traversals records progress from both between quanta, and cancellation never requires more than the existing 65,536 logical-element interval; resumable traversal cleanup is exact under OOM at every allocation site.

Repeated definitions/use-order changes/module registrations/aliases under concurrent resolution keep allocator live bytes bounded by current snapshots, cells, live generations, and active readers rather than total update count; teardown frees every retained chunk.

The process intern table uses blocking contention rather than a tryLock spin while preserving returned IDs, getBytes round-trip, idempotent reinterning, cancellation during hashing/probing, and append-only segment behavior through public interfaces.
`attempt` remains an in-machine boundary and is observationally equivalent to spawn+await over ordinary success/language-failure quotations; it does not start workers during the soul test.

Task-cell completion, environment binding publication, registry swaps, and provenance publication have Release/Acquire visibility and the named Linux TSan suite is green under high-contention spawn/await/cancel/parse/load/module/output stress.

The focused ordinary suite covers low-level allocation failures, while `zig build test-oom` performs one initialized-Session one-worker sweep through all task surfaces; child OOM propagates as OutOfMemory, every worker is joined, and no language error dict is fabricated.

`zig build test`, ReleaseSafe, ReleaseFast, `zig build test-workers`, `zig build test-oom`, `zig build test-tsan`, `zig build differential`, the frozen oracle differential, `zig fmt --check .`, ZLint --deny-warnings, and `zig build source-audit` are green.

The source audit reports scheduler/concurrency <=3,500 business-logic lines, kernels/idioms <=8,500, every budgeted business-logic component within its recorded strong-type/resumable-state cap, and total shipped business-logic Zig <=30,000; tests, fixtures, build/source-audit verification tooling, and all `.ecl` source remain uncapped and no test reads implementation files to assert substrings.

explicitOpinions.opinion: The Session, not each REPL line, owns the root TaskScope.
explicitOpinions.rationale: d.20 names the REPL session as the root and tasks must remain awaitable across runUnit calls. A line-owned scope would cancel every unawaited spawn before the prompt could return and make the concurrency surface useless interactively.

explicitOpinions.opinion: Use one mutex-protected intrusive FIFO before any work-stealing design.
explicitOpinions.rationale: The architecture explicitly licenses the simple global queue for v1. Intrusive Unit links avoid allocation/relocation on enqueue and focus the correctness proof on movable units, parking, and exactly-once wakeup.

explicitOpinions.opinion: One exact-size WaitSet owns every registration for one park and one mutex-serialized, single-winner wake reason.
explicitOpinions.rationale: Completion, timeout, and cancellation can otherwise enqueue the same Unit twice. A per-park object also lets the winner unlink all losing task/timer registrations before the Unit resumes, so stale list nodes never reference reused Unit state.

explicitOpinions.opinion: await-any prevalidates completely, scans already-done tasks left-to-right, and uses scheduler timing only after registration.
explicitOpinions.rationale: This prevents partial waiter registration on a later type error and gives deterministic semantics whenever no actual race is required. Duplicate handles naturally resolve to their lowest index.

explicitOpinions.opinion: await-for timeout never cancels its task.
explicitOpinions.rationale: A deadline limits one wait, not the lifetime of a first-class handle. The caller can later await, cancel, or pass the task elsewhere; conflating timeout with cancellation would make a read operation destructive and break idempotent task semantics.

explicitOpinions.opinion: tasks returns pending descendants in deterministic spawn preorder.
explicitOpinions.rationale: The research contract describes a walk of the live tree rather than only direct children. Spawn preorder makes reflection stable without constraining execution order; each retained handle is rechecked before materialization so terminal tasks are omitted.

explicitOpinions.opinion: Snapshot reclamation uses per-publication reader leases rather than one scheduler-global epoch.
explicitOpinions.rationale: Environment and Registry already have stable cells plus atomic current snapshots. A local reader count gives each structure an explicit lifetime contract, works for non-scheduler/bootstrap callers, and reclaims complete retired chains without coupling namespace lookup to worker epochs.

explicitOpinions.opinion: Every scheduler-owned unknown-size collection is intrusive or fixed-chunked.
explicitOpinions.rationale: Ready queues, waiter lists, child lists, and the timer heap are live synchronization structures. Avoiding relocating growth keeps pointers stable, makes cancellation unlink allocation-free, and follows the bounded-work infrastructure already adopted across the runtime.

explicitOpinions.opinion: One console lease covers rendering, bytes, newline, and flush for a logical call.
explicitOpinions.rationale: Locking individual chunks prevents a data race but still interleaves a value or line. The language promises cross-task ordering is unspecified, not that individual calls may be torn apart.

explicitOpinions.opinion: Child OutOfMemory is a terminal scheduler state that re-propagates host OutOfMemory on await.
explicitOpinions.rationale: The existing interpreter deliberately excludes OOM from d.19 language outcomes and attempt does not catch it. Fabricating an 'err dict for a child would make spawn+await observably catch failures that synchronous execution cannot catch.

explicitOpinions.opinion: ECL_WORKERS is strict positive configuration and never a semantic feature flag.
explicitOpinions.rationale: Silently falling back on malformed input defeats reproducible debugging, while maintaining behavior branches by worker count would contradict determinism-at-join-points. The worker matrix treats every valid count as the same language.

explicitOpinions.opinion: par-each remains documented target-language source in v1 and spawns one task per element.
explicitOpinions.rationale: The vocabulary marks it [E], and the workstream's chunking license preserves a future primitive override without requiring one now. The source body is the readable semantic authority; documentation warns that its intended grains are coarse and independent.

explicitOpinions.opinion: Concurrency tests observe runtime behavior, allocator ownership, outputs, and public counters; source rules stay in the parsed source audit.
explicitOpinions.rationale: This preserves AGENTS.md's prohibition on implementation-substring tests while still enforcing exact file classification, business-logic-only line ceilings, ECL exclusion, and non-relocating scheduler architecture in the dedicated uncapped build tool.

explicitOpinions.opinion: Line ceilings constrain shipped business logic only; tests and verification tooling remain exactly classified but uncapped.
explicitOpinions.rationale: A product-complexity budget should not discourage behavioral coverage or the build tooling that enforces architecture. Tests, fixtures, inline test declarations, build/source-audit verification code, and target-language ECL therefore consume no component or total Zig allowance.

explicitOpinions.opinion: str and pp render tasks as stable per-Session <task:N> markers, and parse rejects any such runtime marker even inside a rendered enclosing structure.
explicitOpinions.rationale: A task is a capability linked to live Session state, not serializable data. Rejecting its display form keeps parse pure and prevents stale or forged IDs; no escaping, surrogate value, or session-local reader lookup is warranted. DESIGN d.16 therefore applies only to values containing no session-linked runtime object.

explicitOpinions.opinion: Every user-sized traversal has one cursor implementation, and a scheduler-attached driver must yield within its accounted-work quantum with that state preserved.
explicitOpinions.rationale: This remains cooperative scheduling at mandatory safe points, but makes the one-worker configuration genuinely fair: a large native word cannot monopolize the worker or prevent another task from running cancellation. Blocking bootstrap and tooling shells drive those same cursors, so no unlimited or cancellation-only implementation can diverge from runtime behavior.

explicitOpinions.opinion: Process exit is a capability of the root Unit outside attempt; tasks communicate outcomes and never terminate the process themselves.
explicitOpinions.rationale: The root owns process lifetime, descendant cancellation, quiescence, and final disposal. Allowing children to race on a Session-global exit status would add scheduler-dependent behavior and bypass ownership; treating exit as task-local success would discard its status semantics. A catchable 'domain outcome lets the root inspect a child's request and decide policy explicitly.

changes: Implement Scheduler.Config with a positive fixed worker count, but do not start workers in init. ensureStarted allocates every worker descriptor before spawning any thread, rolls back/join-stops a partially started pool, and creates no timer. Implement TaskCell as a heap-owned write-once state with one mutex, outcome/OOM terminal arms, ordered child links, cancel flag, and waiter list. Complete under the mutex, move waiters out, Release-publish terminal state, then process wakeups without holding the cell lock. A task retains itself for its executing Unit and parent scope so dropping user handles cannot free live work.

Implement exact-size WaitSet/WaitRegistration ownership and a mutex-serialized pending/completion/cancel policy. Registration links are doubly linked for allocation-free removal. The winner records its reason, schedules bounded unlink and release work, transitions Unit parked->ready once, and only then enqueues; losers retire registrations and never touch Unit stacks.

Implement TaskScope close: set closing/cancel, recursively flag pending descendants under per-cell locks with parent-before-child discipline, perform the post-registration kill-on-arrival check, and park a spawned owner until its child count reaches zero. Session root close blocks the caller on a condition, then workers stop only after the root is quiescent.

The lease is movable only by ownership and always unlocks through defer; Patch 4 will route language writers and Patch 6 main writers through it. changes: spawn validates/consumes a quotation, constructs the child Unit with an empty stack and lazy isolated Scope parented to the current scope, registers it under the current TaskScope, rechecks cancellation, starts the pool lazily, and returns the retained task Value. changes: await-any consumes and fully scans a nonempty generic/list value before mutating any cell. Retain an exact array of task headers; reject non-list as type, empty as domain, and any non-task as type with the outer transaction unchanged. Scan terminal states left-to-right and return the first immediately; otherwise build one WaitSet with ordered registrations and park.

On concurrent completion, each cell detaches registrations in bounded slices after terminal publication; the WaitSet policy records exactly one registration's zero-based index/outcome. The winner schedules resumable loser unlinking before one owner enqueue. Duplicate handles preserve lowest-index behavior through the exact canonical directory; a loser never overwrites the winner.

await-for validates a nonnegative integer milliseconds and checks terminal state before the deadline. Convert with checked arithmetic to a monotonic timestamp; exact 0 times out only if still pending. Register one task waiter and one timer node sharing the same WaitSet token. Completion removes the timer node; timeout removes the cell waiter; timeout materialization is a normal d.19 outcome and leaves the task pending.

Start one timer thread only on the first pending deadline. Store heap nodes in indexed fixed chunks so swaps update stable node indices without relocating entries. A mutex plus wake epoch lets a newly earlier deadline interrupt the wait; deletion is O(log n), charged before parking, and stop wakes/joins immediately regardless of the minimum deadline.

mergabilityInsight: 3 of 6 patches are INFRA. The scheduler's shared state machine intentionally forms a linear dependency chain: Patch 1 hardens publications and creates all pending proofs; Patch 2 makes values/Units/scopes suspendable; Patch 3 installs an unreachable pool/cell/wait/console core; Patches 4-6 then expose basic tasks, races/timers, and par-each/acceptance in order. There is no flag, migration, external service, benchmark gate, operator action, or unresolved semantic branch; each patch has one unconditional contract and the gameplan is autonomous.
finalStateSpec:
module SCHEDULER_AND_CONCURRENCY.

> M7 adds first-class identity tasks scheduled as movable green Units on one
> lazy fixed worker pool. Await parks Units on write-once multi-waiter cells;
> completion, cancellation, and timeout race through one winner token. Parent
> scopes cancel and quiesce descendants. Safe points preserve cursor state,
> console calls are whole writes, and deterministic joins agree at all worker
> counts. Snapshot publication is reader-leased and reclaiming.

---
> Task values are identity-bearing and await is cached.
all a: Task, b: Task | match-task (task-value a) (task-value b) = (identity a = identity b).
all t: Task | await t = await t.
all t: Task | parseable (render-task t) = false.
all t: Task | parseable (nested-task-render t) = false.

> Process exit belongs only to the root Unit outside attempt and quiesces first.
all r: ExitRequest, root-unit (issuer r) = false | exit-disposition r = domain-failure.
all r: ExitRequest, inside-attempt r | exit-disposition r = domain-failure.
all r: ExitRequest, root-unit (issuer r), inside-attempt r = false | exit-disposition r = process-exit.
all r: ExitRequest, exit-disposition r = process-exit | root-quiescent r.

> Spawn isolates execution and parked Units consume no worker.
all q: Quotation, s: Scope | parent-scope (spawn q s) = s.
all q: Quotation, s: Scope | execution-scope (spawn q s) ~= s.
all u: Unit, parked u | occupies-worker u = false.
all w: Wait | enqueue-count (wait-unit w) <= 1.
all w: Work, scheduler-attached w | steps-before-return w <= quantum.

> Cancellation and task reflection obey structured lifetime.
all t: Task, cancelled t | await t = cancel-outcome t.
all s: Scope, t: Task, in-list t (tasks s) | pending t.

> await-any returns one in-range indexed task and timeout is non-destructive.
all l: TaskList, list-count l > 0 | any-index l < list-count l.
all l: TaskList, list-count l > 0 | await-any l = await (list-item l (any-index l)).
all t: Task, d: DurationMs, await-for t d = timeout-outcome | cancelled t = false.

> Successful par-each preserves order/cardinality and failure is leftmost.
all s: Sequence, q: Quotation, succeeds (par-each s q) | count (par-result (par-each s q)) = count s.
all s: Sequence, q: Quotation, i: Nat0, i < count s, leftmost-failure s q i | par-each s q = error-at s q i.

> Deterministic programs are worker-count invariant and cold execution is lazy.
all source: Quotation, a: WorkerCount, b: WorkerCount | stdout (run source a) = stdout (run source b).
all source: Quotation, a: WorkerCount, b: WorkerCount | stderr (run source a) = stderr (run source b).
all source: Quotation, a: WorkerCount, b: WorkerCount | status (run source a) = status (run source b).
all source: Quotation, w: WorkerCount, uses-spawn source = false | worker-threads (run source w) = 0.

> Reader leases prohibit early reclamation and permit retired cleanup.
all p: Publication, r: Reader, s: Snapshot, holds r s | reclaimed p s = false.
all p: Publication, s: Snapshot, retired p s, unheld s | reclaimed p s.
